alt: A three-row table for the if, elif, and else conditions of the shipping-cost formula, checked from top to bottom. The row whose condition is first true is marked as the winner, and the rows below it are never checked.

steps.caption: The cost is 10. Python checks the first condition: is it at most 20?
It is. A cost of 10 takes the if branch right away, and the elif and else are skipped entirely.
The cost is 30. Python checks the first condition: is it at most 20?
A cost of 30 is over 20, so Python moves on to the elif: is it at most 50?
It is. The elif branch runs here, so the else never gets a turn.
The cost is 60. Python checks the first condition: is it at most 20?
A cost of 60 is over 20, so Python moves on to the elif: is it at most 50?
A cost of 60 is over 50 too, so neither the if nor the elif ever matched. Whatever is left over runs the else.
